title: Sensor divider: darkness switches the lamp on
subject: electronics

scenes.caption: Bright daylight: the circuit assembles, lamp off
scenes.narration: A 6 V supply drives a fixed resistor and an LDR in series, and the output is taken across the LDR. In bright daylight the LDR resistance is low, so it takes only a small share of the supply and the lamp stays off.

steps.text: Bright daylight: low LDR resistance, low output, lamp off

scenes.caption: Light falls: resistance steps up, output climbs
scenes.narration: As the light falls the LDR resistance steps up to 1 kΩ, equal to the fixed resistor. Equal resistances split the supply evenly, so the output voltage across the LDR climbs to 3.0 V - still below the threshold.

scenes.caption: Dusk: the output stops just below the threshold
scenes.narration: At dusk the LDR resistance steps up again to 2.3 kΩ, more than twice the fixed resistor. Its share of the supply climbs to 4.2 V - close to, but still just below, the 4.5 V threshold, so the lamp stays off.

scenes.caption: Dark: the output crosses the threshold and the lamp lights
scenes.narration: In the dark the LDR resistance rises to 9 kΩ, nine times the fixed resistor, so it takes 5.4 V of the 6 V supply. The output crosses the 4.5 V threshold and switches the lamp on - the bigger resistance always takes the bigger share.
